title: AI Hackers Are Faster Than Your Pen Test — Eli Cohen, Snyk
talk_summary: Eli Cohen argues that AI-generated code and AI attackers make periodic pentesting obsolete, so security must run continuously on every PR with LLM agents. He describes a vendor pipeline of orchestrator, recon, specialized vulnerability testers, an exploit-validation judge, remediation, and reporting, fed by static/dynamic scanner context.

takeaways.what_they_do: A separate judge agent receives every finding from vulnerability-testing agents and decides whether it is real and exploitable before reporting it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every vulnerability that the previous agent find are now being handed over to this judge

takeaways.what_they_do: Run AI pentesting on every code change, PR, and delta instead of a few times per year.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We're going to do it on every code change. Okay? Every PR that you send, every delta
takeaways.numbers: fastest AI attack cited: 4 minutes; average 24-34 minutes

takeaways.technique: Feed scanner context into LLM reviewer
takeaways.what_they_do: Combine static scanner, dynamic scanner, and agent-engine outputs as context so the LLM knows where to look.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we actually feed it with data from all the previous scanners

takeaways.what_they_do: An LLM orchestrator follows a dynamic plan and operates subagents: recon maps endpoints/APIs, specialized testers hunt classes of bugs, then judge and remediation agents process findings.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This agent is working according to a dynamic plan that it follows and it knows how to operate all the different sub agents.

takeaways.what_they_do: A remediation agent converts validated findings into concrete fixes, and a reporting agent packages results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: remediation agent because everything we do we want to make actionable

takeaways.technique: Combine scanners instead of relying on one
takeaways.what_they_do: Use multiple scanner classes together because each is best at different vulnerability types, then combine their data for the LLM.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one solution is not enough. Okay. The great thing about it is when you combine those things together
